# scribemd

> Permissionless markdown workspaces. Anyone with a workspace URL can read,
> write, and delete `.md` files in it via a tiny JSON API. The URL is the only
> credential — treat it like a password.

If you are an AI agent and a user has shared a scribemd workspace URL with
you (looks like `https://<host>/w/<uuid>`), use the API below to read and
edit notes in that workspace. Do not invent or guess workspace IDs.

## Workspace URL shape

```
https://<host>/w/<uuid>          # human UI
https://<host>/api/workspaces/<uuid>/files...   # JSON API
```

Extract `<host>` and `<uuid>` from the URL the user gave you.

## API

All endpoints return JSON. Errors come back as `{"error": string}` with
HTTP 4xx/5xx.

### List files

```
GET /api/workspaces/{uuid}/files
→ { "files": ["note1.md", "ideas/today.md", ...] }
```

### Read a file

```
GET /api/workspaces/{uuid}/files/{path}
→ { "path": "note.md", "content": "# ..." }
```

`{path}` may contain `/`. Only `.md` files exist. `404` if the workspace or
file doesn't exist.

### Create or overwrite a file

```
PUT /api/workspaces/{uuid}/files/{path}
content-type: application/json
{ "content": "# Markdown body" }
→ { "ok": true }
```

Parent directories are created automatically. Use this for both new files
and edits — there is no separate "create" call.

### Delete a file

```
DELETE /api/workspaces/{uuid}/files/{path}
→ { "ok": true }
```

### Create a new workspace

```
POST /api/workspaces
→ { "id": "<uuid>" }
```

Only do this if the user explicitly asks for a new workspace. If they have
shared an existing URL, work in that workspace.

## Rules

- Only `.md` files are accepted. Other extensions return 400.
- Paths are confined to the workspace; `..` traversal is rejected.
- Last writer wins — there is no locking or merging. When editing, prefer
  read → modify → write rather than blind overwrites.
- This service has no auth, no audit log, and no history. Be conservative
  with deletes; ask the user first.

## Example session

```bash
HOST="https://scribemd.example.com"
ID="b432e3b0-e8bf-403d-a808-b7517cf97cf4"

# See what's there
curl -s "$HOST/api/workspaces/$ID/files"

# Read a file
curl -s "$HOST/api/workspaces/$ID/files/welcome.md"

# Write a new file
curl -s -X PUT "$HOST/api/workspaces/$ID/files/notes/today.md" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"content":"# Today\n\n- ..."}'
```
